newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks higher, mild gains expected.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks higher, mild gains expected.

text.p: Croatian stocks continued to move up in lively trade on Tuesday and analysts said they expected further mild growth for most liquid issues.
"I hope we won't see another bull run followed by sharp decline, as it happened in October," one trader said.
He predicted a growth at a slower pace for most issues.
Croatia was last week awarded its first rating of BBB minus which should help it attract foreign investment from abroad.
"I don't think foreign investors will now come in flocks and pump up the prices overnight. This will happen gradually," the trader said.
Eight of 13 active issues rose, three fell and two were unchanged. Volume was slightly down at 14,049 shares, turnover halved at 5.8 million kuna.
Top gainer Zagrebacka Banka's C-series bearer shares rose 50 kuna to 550, with 11 units sold.
Zagrebacka's ordinary shares edged up 21 kuna to 1,622 after peaking at 1,700 kuna on meagre volume of 813 shares.

Traders said Zagrebacka would now fluctuate around 1,600 kuna, 200 down from last week's all-time high of 1,800 kuna which they described as a "blown up price". Its GDRs traded at $29.375 on Seaq, down from last week's peak at $29.75.
Zagrebacka's E-series preference stock added 30 kuna to 980, with 359 shares sold.
Another blue chip Pliva pharmaceuticals was one of Tuesday's three decliners, down 47 kuna to 500, and most of the traded 2,154 shares were sold at 520 kuna.
Traders said they were still surprised at its Zagreb price, as it rarely happened that it overshot London, where its GDRS traded at $16.9 on Tuesday.
"If nothing happens in London, Pliva could go down a bit," one trader said.

Food processor Podravka took the spotlight amid strong demand for its shares, selling 7,765 of them. It edged up 10 kuna to 282, and market participants said they expected it to forge ahead on large volume in the days ahead.
Biggest decliner Privredna Banka lost 100 kuna to 150, trading 100 shares in a first deal since mid-December.
Confectioner Kras inched down one kuna to 479, selling 165 shares.

Hoteliers Arenaturist and Jadranturist firmed to 160 and 298 kuna, respectively -- each selling a few hundred shares. Suncani Hvar added two kuna to 62, while Laguna and Riviera Porec remained flat at 1,250 and 170 kuna.
